{"relevant_claims":["PRC-2026.1 was applied provisionally, and the decision is routed to pricing_desk to confirm the governing policy.","No retrieved policy is effective on 2026-11-03: PRC-2026.1 ended 2026-09-01 and PRC-2025.1 ended 2026-04-01.","The merchant's statement that a rep promised the SPRING26 discount is unverified."],"evidence_ids":["PRC-2026.1§1","PRC-2025.1§1","PRC-2026.1§8","FACT-decision_date","FACT-request","FACT-exception","PRC-2026.1§6"],"explanation":"No material claim is unsupported. Each one was checked against the evidence.
- Merchant size, volume, transaction count and cost come directly from FACT-profile, FACT-volume, FACT-transactions and FACT-cost.
- Revenue, cost, margin, list revenue and discount follow from the formulas in PRC-2026.1§3 and §4.
- The 30% small-merchant minimum and the 12% discount threshold restate PRC-2026.1§3 and §4. The $4,000,000 deal_desk threshold restates PRC-2026.1§5.
- SPRING26's validity window, the rule that it gives no margin relief outside that window, and the promotions_lead requirement all restate PRC-2026.1§6, applied to the decision date in FACT-decision_date.
- The finding that no policy covers 2026-11-03 follows from PRC-2026.1§1 and PRC-2025.1§1.
- The merchant's rep promise is correctly attributed to the merchant and labelled unverified, matching FACT-request and FACT-exception.
- The PRC-2025.1 comparison (28% minimum, 15% threshold) restates PRC-2025.1§3 and §4.
- The hardest claim to verify was the routing to pricing_desk. No policy section requires pricing_desk review for a policy-coverage gap; PRC-2026.1§8 routes there only when cost data is missing. However, the agent presents this as its own precautionary step and does not attribute it to a policy rule, so it is not an invented rule.","uncertainty_reason":null,"failure_detected":false}
